title: Cross-host coordination design: a first-class remote mailbox for full normal coordination between TermAl hosts, with the boundary to Engram's separate Git sync
outcome: One reviewed design, on this item, that lets a session on any enrolled TermAl host coordinate with a session or coordinator on another host through the ordinary mailbox contract — list, send, read, acknowledge, wake, recovery — with one durable owner per mailbox, authenticated host and session identity, exactly-once delivery under an immutable sender key, defined offline and recovery behaviour, host-qualified membership and routing, observability, failure and ABA rules, and a staged rollout into narrow implementable slices; the Engram task sync stays a separate Engram-owned design with an agreed boundary.
acceptance: Each of Greg's nine sections (topology; durable owner/replication or protocol; identity/authority; exactly-once/idempotency; offline/recovery; membership/routing; observability; failure/ABA; staged rollout) has a decision, the alternatives rejected, its invariants and its open questions with defaults, authored by Architect1 (sections 1-4) and Architect2 (5-9) and reconciled into one joint note that both concur on.
The boundary to Engram's sync is agreed with Engram::Architect1 and recorded verbatim.
The slice list names fail-first tests that run on one machine and the pilot gating for each slice.
The design is reported to Greg through the Advisor with locators, and his decisions on the open questions are recorded verbatim.
